dimensions.name: GROUNDING
findings: behavioral-spec.md 'Scope of the strategy program' section and REQ-DL2's rationale both assert 'openevolve's own scoping guarantee (ch08 agent3 finding) means it structurally cannot propose edits there' / 'This is openevolve's own structural guarantee.' I re-verified against the real algorithmicsuperintelligence/openevolve source (gh api, files read directly): controller.py:_load_initial_program() does `with open(...) as f: return f.read()` — the WHOLE file, not just the EVOLVE-BLOCK content; prompt/templates.py's DIFF_USER_TEMPLATE shows the LLM the entire `current_program` (full file) with zero instruction to restrict edits to the marked region ('Focus on making targeted changes' is the only guidance, no mention of EVOLVE-BLOCK at all); process_parallel.py's diff-based path calls `apply_diff(parent.code, llm_response, ...)` which does a SEARCH/REPLACE match against the ENTIRE `parent.code`, not scoped to marker line-ranges; the full-rewrite path (`diff_based_evolution: false`, still a real, documented config option) does `child_code = new_code` — a literal whole-file replacement. `parse_evolve_blocks()` exists in utils/code_utils.py and is exported, but is NEVER called from process_parallel.py, controller.py, or api.py's main iteration path — it is dead code with respect to enforcement. Conclusion: openevolve provides ZERO technical/structural enforcement of EVOLVE-BLOCK scope; the markers are a human/prompt-level convention only. This is the same class of error ch08 caught elsewhere (claiming a repo mechanism exists when it doesn't) and it is reintroduced here as a load-bearing architectural claim.

REQ-OE5 cites Sutton & Barto §2.4 ('appropriate in a stationary environment, but not if the bandit is changing over time' — verified verbatim against the actual PDF via firecrawl) to justify `database.num_islands >= 2` / MAP-Elites diversity as 'the openevolve-native answer to ch08 deviation (a)'. But Sutton & Barto's own prescribed remedy in that exact section is recency-weighting ('it makes sense to weight recent rewards more heavily'), not population diversity / multi-island evolutionary search. openevolve's own docs (configs/README.md: 'num_islands: 3-10 for most problems (more = more diversity)') justify islands purely as premature-convergence/diversity maintenance for evolutionary search — an unrelated mechanism. The spec's real (and actually adequate) answer to non-stationarity is REQ-EV3/RH5's freshly-rotated walk-forward windows per run, not the islands mechanism; citing Sutton & Barto for REQ-OE5 specifically is a citation-fit error, not merely imprecise phrasing.

dimensions.name: COMPLETENESS
findings: /goal Done condition (5) 'LOOP 1 one human-zero cycle self-merges' is not addressed anywhere in behavioral-spec.md or verification-architecture.md. The spec's own Purpose section states it builds 'LOOP 2's self-improve mechanism' (09-cobus-adoption.md terminology), and 09's LOOP 1 is claude-p's separate Schedule->self-Triage->...->自merge->Monitor->Seed loop — a different loop entirely. Nowhere does the spec say what triggers an openevolve run (cron/LOOP 1 self-triage vs. a human manually invoking run_evolve.sh), so it is unverifiable whether goal condition (5) is even in scope for this feature, or whether — absent any scheduling requirement — a human is implicitly needed to kick off each cycle (which would itself violate INV-1). This ambiguity must be resolved explicitly (either: state condition (5) refers to this feature's OWN git branch self-merge per standing project process and cite that, or add a REQ specifying the autonomous trigger/schedule for run_evolve.sh).

/goal Done condition (1) 'fresh adversary PASS on spec AND impl' is only partially covered. The 'Done'/4-D Convergence table's `verification` row folds a fresh adversary PASS into 'that specific diff' (i.e., a runtime, per-candidate promotion gate, REQ-RH4 step 3) — this is a different adversary invocation than the standard VCSDD Phase-3 'impl' review of THIS FEATURE'S OWN source code (gate_math.py, scope_guard.py, evaluator.py, promote.py, run_evolve.sh), which project rule .claude/rules/dev-workflow.md requires (codex-review + vcsdd-adversary after 5+ files implemented, before commit/PR/release). The spec's Done table never names this second, distinct adversary gate explicitly — a builder could satisfy the letter of the Done table (candidate-level adversary PASS) while skipping the actual code-quality/architecture review of the harness itself.

verification-architecture.md PROP-SI-EV2's property statement is incoherent and not implementable as written: 'evaluate_stage1 score is monotonically no-better than evaluate_stage2's in-sample score is expected to differ from its out-of-sample score (sanity: stage1 window ⊂ stage2 windows)' runs two unrelated clauses together with no coherent grammar/logic; a builder cannot derive a single concrete pytest assertion from this sentence as given. Needs to be rewritten as one well-formed, testable predicate.

dimensions.name: BP CONFORMANCE
findings: Weng/Zelikman's STOP cautionary finding ('STOP improved performance with GPT-4 but DEGRADED with weaker models (GPT-3.5, Mixtral)', per docs/loop-engineering/06-harness-engineering-weng.md line 40, and the file's own prescribed mitigation 'adversary(強モデル)+bounded surface を厳守する') is never cited or explicitly addressed anywhere in behavioral-spec.md, despite REQ-OE4 explicitly configuring the improver LLM to a free-tier/ClawRouter model (i.e., precisely the 'weaker model' regime the STOP warning is about). The architecture happens to partially mitigate the risk by accident (REQ-EV1's deterministic, non-LLM evaluator; REQ-RH4's strong-model — Sonnet, per project model-assignment table — adversary gate before promotion), but this mitigation is not identified, cited, or justified as a deliberate response to the STOP finding anywhere in the spec's sources/rationale, violating the project's own citation discipline ('判断には最低1つの引用...を付ける') for exactly the concern the review brief calls out.

Deviation (a) (non-stationary bandit) and (b) (reward-hacking) are otherwise well handled (Beta-bandit dropped per REQ-GR4; capping/trip-wire/sandbox present per REQ-RH1-RH3) and deviation (c) (validation vs. allocation layering) is reasonably scoped-out (no cross-strategy bandit is built in this phase at all) — these are not separately blocking, but are noted as partial credit; the STOP-warning gap above is the blocking BP item.

dimensions.name: CONSISTENCY & SAFETY
findings: INV-3 states 'Denylist (REQ-DL1) MUST be enforced structurally via EVOLVE-BLOCK scoping + the defensive diff-scope/checksum/import-scan checks (REQ-DL2-DL4)' — as established under GROUNDING, EVOLVE-BLOCK scoping provides no enforcement at all in real openevolve; 100% of the actual safety guarantee rests on the wrapper's own REQ-DL2/DL3/DL4 checks operating against the ACTUAL resulting candidate file (child_code) versus the baseline, not against the LLM's raw diff text framed as 'defense in depth' on top of a real primary guarantee. The spec must be corrected to say the wrapper checks ARE the entire enforcement (not a backup), and REQ-DL2 in particular must be specified against the file-level diff between child_code and the baseline (which REQ-DL3's checksum approach does correctly by construction), not against 'a proposed program diff' ambiguously (the raw LLM SEARCH/REPLACE text, which in full-rewrite mode doesn't even exist as a line-scoped diff). This is not a wording nit given the stakes (wallet keys, spend caps, ledger-write path) — an implementer trusting the spec's framing could under-build scope_guard.py believing openevolve already blocks most bad cases.

Because pick.py (per the actual file read) contains the wallet/order-execution-adjacent import surface (AGENT_HOME-based src.* modules) and 'the harness that calls this file' in the SAME file as the EVOLVE-BLOCK, and because the whole file is shown verbatim to a free-tier LLM as established under GROUNDING, the free-tier improver model directly sees this adjacent code every generation. The spec does not acknowledge this exposure or consider splitting sensitive code into a separate, never-shown module — a stronger design given the money-safety stakes.

dimensions.name: OVERCLAIM/HONESTY
findings: The claim 'openevolve's own scoping guarantee... means it structurally cannot propose edits there' is stated as an established fact (not flagged UNVERIFIED) despite being false per direct source inspection (see GROUNDING). The spec's own UNVERIFIED section only flags 'exact upstream config field names' and 'pick.py's exact function boundary' as needing re-confirmation — it does NOT flag the enforcement-mechanism claim itself, which is the single most safety-critical claim in the document. This is the exact honesty failure mode ch08 was written to correct (asserting a mechanism's protective property as fact without re-verifying it against the real source), reintroduced in a new form.

'residual risk: money is still a proxy (Goodhart)' is honestly acknowledged in spirit via REQ-RH1/RH2/RH5 (capping, trip-wire, walk-forward-overfitting guard) and is consistent with ch08 §B item (b) — this part is done honestly and is not itself a finding.

'mirrors the stripForbidden() pattern already proven in genome.mjs' (REQ-DL2) and the evaluatePromotion/KNOB_KEYS/FORBIDDEN_CAP_KEYS/ledger.mjs internal citations were checked directly against skills/earn/lib/genome.mjs, evolve.mjs, skills/_shared/lib/ledger.mjs, skills/earn/polymarket-trade/pick.py and skills/earn/baseline-genome.json in the worktree — all exist and match as described (KNOB_KEYS, FORBIDDEN_CAP_KEYS, stripForbidden, evaluatePromotion's net-positive-floor logic, ledger.mjs's four named exports). These internal citations are NOT misattributed — noted as a positive finding, not a gap.

dimensions.name: IMPLEMENTABILITY
findings: The 'Grounded Interface' table (evaluate/EvaluationResult, cascade evaluate_stage1/evaluate_stage2 via hasattr module inspection, cascade_thresholds under EvaluatorConfig, database.population_size/num_islands, llm.primary_model/api_base, run_evolution/openevolve-run.py) was independently verified against the real openevolve source (openevolve/evaluation_result.py, openevolve/config.py, openevolve/evaluator.py, openevolve/api.py) and is ACCURATE — this part of the spec is implementable as described. This is a positive finding, not a gap.

However, REQ-OE2/OE3's premise — that pick.py has (or can trivially be given) a `score_candidate(candidate, market_features, config) -> float` pure, backtestable EVOLVE-BLOCK region — does not match the actual pick.py read directly from the worktree: its docstring states 'NOTHING about WHICH market or WHICH side is hardcoded here... The MODEL decides' via `get_analyzer().consensus_analysis` (a live, multi-model LLM inference call over 3 BlockRun models) plus `fetch_active_markets`/`get_smart_money_summary` (live network/market-data calls). The core 'judgment' this file makes is NOT a static function of pre-fetched market_features; it is a live LLM-consensus call baked into the decision path. Building a backtestable EVOLVE-BLOCK-scoped pure function out of this requires either (a) caching/replaying historical LLM-consensus outputs per candidate window (a nontrivial data pipeline not specified anywhere in the spec), or (b) redesigning the evolvable unit to exclude the LLM-consensus call entirely (changing what 'the strategy' even means for evolution purposes) — neither approach is specified. The spec's UNVERIFIED section ('pick.py's exact function boundary... was not re-read line-by-line') materially understates this: it is not a boundary-drawing question, it is an unresolved architecture question that blocks writing evaluator.py at all.

blockingFindings: 1. GROUNDING — behavioral-spec.md 'Scope of the strategy program' section + REQ-DL2 rationale claim 'openevolve's own scoping guarantee... means it structurally cannot propose edits there' / 'this is openevolve's own structural guarantee.' Verified FALSE by reading openevolve/controller.py (_load_initial_program reads whole file via f.read()), openevolve/prompt/templates.py (LLM shown the entire current_program, no marker-respecting instruction), and openevolve/process_parallel.py (apply_diff operates over the whole parent.code; full-rewrite mode sets child_code = new_code, the entire file). parse_evolve_blocks() exists but is dead code w.r.t. enforcement. Fix: rewrite this claim to state plainly that openevolve provides NO structural enforcement of EVOLVE-BLOCK scope, and that 100% of the safety guarantee comes from this feature's own scope_guard.py.

2. GROUNDING — REQ-OE5 cites Sutton & Barto §2.4 to justify database.num_islands>=2 as 'the openevolve-native answer to ch08 deviation (a)', but §2.4's own prescribed fix is recency-weighting, not population diversity/MAP-Elites (a different, openevolve-native-but-unrelated mechanism per openevolve's own configs/README.md). Fix: cite openevolve's own diversity rationale for REQ-OE5, and rely on REQ-EV3/RH5 (rotated walk-forward windows) — already in the spec — as the actual, correctly-grounded answer to non-stationarity.

3. COMPLETENESS — /goal Done condition (5) 'LOOP 1 one human-zero cycle self-merges' is not addressed anywhere in the spec; it is unclear whether this refers to this feature's own dev-branch self-merge (standing process) or an autonomous trigger/schedule for the harness's openevolve runs (unaddressed — no REQ specifies what triggers run_evolve.sh, risking a hidden human-in-the-loop). Fix: add an explicit REQ/clarifying note resolving this.

4. COMPLETENESS — /goal Done condition (1)'s 'impl' adversary PASS conflates the per-candidate runtime adversary gate (REQ-RH4 step 3) with the standard VCSDD Phase-3 review of this feature's own source code; the Done table never names the latter explicitly. Fix: add a distinct Done-table row/condition for a Phase-3 vcsdd-adversary PASS on the harness's own implementation files.

5. BP CONFORMANCE — Weng/Zelikman's STOP warning (weak improver model degrades self-improvement quality; docs/loop-engineering/06-harness-engineering-weng.md line 40) is never cited or explicitly addressed, despite REQ-OE4 configuring exactly the free-tier/weak-model regime the warning is about. Fix: add an explicit citation + rationale (deterministic evaluator + strong-model adversary gate as the mitigation) to the sources/REQ rationale.

6. CONSISTENCY & SAFETY — INV-3's 'enforced structurally via EVOLVE-BLOCK scoping + defensive... checks' is factually inaccurate per finding #1; REQ-DL2 must be respecified to operate on the file-level diff between the actual candidate file and baseline (not 'a proposed program diff' ambiguously, which doesn't exist as a line-scoped object in full-rewrite mode). Fix: rewrite INV-3 and REQ-DL2 to state the wrapper checks are the sole enforcement mechanism.

7. OVERCLAIM/HONESTY — the false EVOLVE-BLOCK-enforcement claim (finding #1) is asserted as established fact, not flagged UNVERIFIED, even though the spec's own UNVERIFIED section demonstrates awareness of exactly this kind of risk for lower-stakes items (config field names, pick.py boundary). Fix: same as #1/#6, plus review the rest of the document for any other claim resembling 'X's own guarantee means Y' before spec-review re-submission.

8. IMPLEMENTABILITY — pick.py (read directly from the worktree) is a live, LLM-consensus-calling, network-fetching script, not a pure `score_candidate(candidate, market_features, config)->float` function as REQ-OE2/OE3 assume; no design is given for how to make it backtestable/evolvable (cache historical consensus outputs? redefine the evolvable unit to exclude the LLM call?). Fix: add an explicit REQ/decision for this refactor before implementation can begin; the current UNVERIFIED note understates this as a 'boundary' question when it is an unresolved architecture question.
summary: FAIL on all 6 dimensions. The spec's grounding on the openevolve interface itself (evaluate/EvaluationResult, cascade stage1/stage2, config fields, run_evolution/openevolve-run.py) is accurate and well-verified — a genuine improvement over the prior eval-driven-earning spec's misattributions, and the Beta-bandit/calibration-drift mechanisms are correctly dropped (REQ-GR4) rather than reintroduced. However the spec reintroduces the SAME class of error in a new place: it asserts as established fact that openevolve structurally enforces the EVOLVE-BLOCK edit boundary, which direct source inspection of controller.py/process_parallel.py/prompt/templates.py shows is false (the markers are convention-only; parse_evolve_blocks() is dead code). This single false claim cascades into failures on Grounding, Consistency & Safety (INV-3's denylist-enforcement claim), and Overclaim/Honesty (asserted as fact, not flagged UNVERIFIED, despite being the single most safety-critical claim in the document). Separately, Completeness fails because /goal condition (5) ('LOOP 1 one human-zero cycle self-merges') is never addressed and the harness's autonomous trigger/schedule is unspecified; BP Conformance fails because Weng's STOP warning about weak-improver-model degradation is never cited despite REQ-OE4 configuring exactly that regime; and Implementability fails because the actual pick.py is a live LLM-consensus script, not the pure backtestable function REQ-OE2/OE3 assume, with no refactor design given. None of these are fatal to the overall approach (openevolve is still the right copy+tweak choice, and most defenses are soundly designed once the enforcement-mechanism claim is corrected) — but the spec needs a revision pass before proceeding to TDD.
